In the Secret Wars episodes that follow, Ock works for the Red Skull and Smythe on Battleworld, not for the Six. The group ends twice, so he belongs to no group after each ending.

Spider-Man (1994): the first Insidious Six disband after season 2 episodes 1-2, and the Chameleon is back in prison. Later he works for Richard Fisk (season 3 episodes 6-7). In 'Six Forgotten Warriors' (season 5) the Kingpin 'decided to band the Insidious Six together again and the other five members broke the Chameleon from S.H.I.E.L.D.', so he rejoins the Six. Only at the Doomsday complex does he gas his teammates and betray them to the Red Skull. The record misses the first disbanding and the rejoin before that betrayal.

Marvel Database files the 1967 Spider-Man animated series as Earth-6799 (designation from the Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe A to Z Vol 1 2); its Earth-67 page is a comics reality described as 'a divergent version of Earth-6799'. The series' characters are filed there, e.g. Matto Magneto (Earth-6799), Fantastic Fakir (Earth-6799), Fifth Avenue Phantom (Earth-6799), Infinata (Earth-6799), Henry Smythe (Earth-6799), Norman Osborn (Earth-6799), Wilson Fisk (Earth-6799), Stan/Lee Patterson (Earth-6799), Curtis Conner (Earth-6799).

Story order is Tricorp, then Oscorp, then the Sinister Six. Otto worked at Tricorp before the series and later came to work for Norman Osborn at Oscorp; in episode 8 ('Reaction') he only breaks into Tricorp's Coney Island R&D building to steal his old Megalopack, so he never rejoins Tricorp after Oscorp. He turns on Osborn after the episode 8 accident and forms the Sinister Six in episode 11 ('Group Therapy'), so the leading Sinister Six stage before Oscorp is also wrong. The final group (The Sinister Six) is unchanged.

Dirk Leyden is a WWI U.S. soldier (backstory, ep 5); after his solo robbery Silvermane springs him from jail and he joins Silvermane's crime ring (ep 5). He is still Silvermane's enforcer when the Spider throws him under a train (ep 8). Marvel Database lists his affiliation as Silvermane's Crime Ring, formerly U.S. Army. He never leaves Silvermane's side before dying, so the last stage 'Independent' is wrong and the order is reversed.

No departure: Leyden fights the Spider alongside Marko on Silvermane's behalf in episode 8 and dies there; death is not a departure. Marko turning on him (to protect Cat) does not remove Leyden from Silvermane's ring.

Montana starts as an Enforcer (S1E1), joins Doc Ock's first Sinister Six (S1E11, ep 11), is left out of the re-formed Six in 'Reinforcement' (S2E3, ep 16; replaced by Mysterio and Kraven), then re-forms the new Enforcers with Ox and Fancy Dan (S2E9) and is in the Vault with them (S2E12, ep 25). Marvel Database: affiliation The Enforcers, formerly Sinister Six. The last stage must be The Enforcers.

After the Chameleon's betrayal and the Red Skull's defeat in 'Six Forgotten Warriors' (S5E2-6, ep 54-58), the Shocker and the rest of the Insidious Six disband; the team is defunct. Marvel Database lists his affiliation as 'Formerly: Insidious Six'. The group ends, so he belongs to no group afterwards.

The reunited Insidious Six (with Rhino) disband at the end of 'Six Forgotten Warriors' (S5E6, ep 58) 'once they realized there was no profit to be made'; team status Defunct. The record's last stage is still The Insidious Six.

Scorpion is in the reunited Insidious Six in 'Six Forgotten Warriors', which disbands at its end (S5E6, ep 58); Marvel Database lists his affiliation as 'Formerly: Insidious Six' and the team as Defunct.

After failing to destroy Spider-Man in 'The Insidious Six'/'Battle of the Insidious Six' (S2E1-2, ep 14-15), the team disbands; Mysterio never rejoins (he is dead by the S5 reunion and is replaced by the Vulture). Marvel Database: affiliation 'Formerly: Wonder Studios, Insidious Six'; 'disbanded to avoid arrest'.

Venom: The Last Dance: General Strickland commands Imperium, the government symbiote operation at Area 51/55, for the whole film; nothing on screen moves him out of Imperium to the military and back (he dies at Area 51 still commanding it). The middle 'U.S. Military' stage and the return to Imperium record moves that never happen.

Spider-Noir: Lonnie's Army service is WWI backstory (revealed in episode 5); in episode 5 he joins Silvermane as an enforcer, and in episode 7 the antidote cures him and he abandons Silvermane and leaves New York. He never goes (back) into the U.S. Army after Silvermane's Mob, so that stage is wrong. The left entry for Spider-Noir stays.

Spider-Man (1994): the Vulture is not in the Insidious Six in his earlier episodes (episodes 27 and 46 on file); he joins only in season 5 ('Six Forgotten Warriors', S5 E2), replacing Mysterio, and the team disbands at the end of that arc (S5 E6) once there is no profit in it. So not 'from the start', and the stage ends when the group ends.

Spider-Man (1994) season 5, episode 6 ('Six Forgotten Warriors' ch. 5): after the Chameleon's betrayal and the Kingpin's defeat, the rest of the Insidious Six disband. The group ends, so add a left entry for Spider-Man (1994).
X-Men '97 season 2 episode 4 (episode 14): Black Widow appears as a member of the Avengers, accompanying Captain America to give Wolverine the Weapon X file.

This villain file is the X-Men '97 Gambit (universe fox, the X-Men animated series). null means Earth-199999 (main MCU), which is wrong; his twin A:fox-anim-gambit and the Marvel Database use Earth-92131.

This villain file is the X-Men: The Animated Series / X-Men '97 Phoenix bonded to that show's Jean Grey (universe fox). null means Earth-199999 (main MCU), which is wrong; the twin A:fox-anim-jean-grey and the Marvel Database use Earth-92131.
The Void Gambit of Deadpool & Wolverine is a pruned variant from the unmade Gambit film's reality, not the main MCU; Marvel Database files him as Remy LeBeau (Earth-TRN1401).

Villain file for the X-Men: The Last Stand / Days of Future Past Jean Grey, the same person as A:fox-jean-grey (Earth-10005). Null wrongly puts her in Earth-199999; Last Stand and the new 2023 of DoFP are Earth-10005 by the owner's rule.
Villain file for Dark Phoenix's Jean Grey, the same person as A:fox-jean-grey-young (Earth-TRN414). Dark Phoenix is Earth-TRN414 by the owner's rule; null wrongly means Earth-199999.

Alex's record runs from X-Men: First Class through DoFP's 1973 and X-Men: Apocalypse, where he dies; his last stand is in Earth-TRN414 under the owner's rule. This matches the young Charles and young Hank records, which are filed Earth-TRN414 even though they start in First Class. (Marvel Database itself keeps Alexander Summers at Earth-10005, which is why this is medium.)

Her file runs from First Class through DoFP's 1973, X-Men: Apocalypse and Dark Phoenix, the young Raven of the TRN414 timeline (the same person as twin A:fox-raven-darkholme, already filed Earth-TRN414). null would make her main-MCU Earth-199999.

In X-Men: First Class, Raven is first with Charles's young mutants at the CIA's Division X and only joins Erik's Brotherhood at the end in Cuba. The leading 'Erik's Mutants' stage, before CIA, is wrong (this matches twin A:fox-raven-darkholme).
X-Men: Apocalypse (1983) is TRN414 under the owner's rule; she is the young Ororo, the same person as twin A:fox-storm-young, already filed Earth-TRN414.

In X-Men: First Class, the CIA's Division X recruits Angel first. She defects to Shaw's Hellfire Club when he attacks the base, and after Shaw dies in Cuba she joins Erik's Brotherhood. The stages are out of order, and the first 'Erik's Mutants' stage is spurious.

In X-Men Origins: Wolverine, Agent Zero is first a member of Stryker's Team X (the opening missions). Later he works for Stryker's Weapon X program, hunting Logan. The leading Weapon X stage, before Team X, is wrong.
The Munsons appear only in Logan (2017). The owner's Fox rule does not cover Logan, and Marvel Database designates the Logan film reality Earth-17315.
The Transigen children appear only in Logan (2017). Marvel Database designates that reality Earth-17315, and Transigen is filed as Transigen (Earth-17315).

Laura comes from the Logan film reality. Marvel Database files her as Laura (Earth-17315) and says the TVA pruned her into the Void from that reality, which Paradox had conflated with Earth-10005, as seen in Deadpool & Wolverine.

X-Men '97 episode 11 (S2E1 'Days of Past Future'): the 3960 Horsemen (Death/Sanjar Javeed, Famine/Jeb Lee, Pestilence/Ichisumi, War/Decimus Furius) serving Apocalypse/Ozymandias are designated Horsemen of Apocalypse (Earth-13393) by Marvel Database, the Askani future, not Earth-92131.

Trask appears only in X-Men: Days of Future Past's 1973 storyline (Sentinel program, White House attack, arrest). Owner rule: Days of Future Past's 1973 is Earth-TRN414 (Marvel Database files him as Earth-10005, but the owner's Fox rule overrides).

Universe is fox but earth is null (= Earth-199999, main MCU). This Blob appears only in Deadpool & Wolverine in the Void; owner rule files Deadpool films as Earth-10005, matching the other D&W Void variants filed on Earth-10005 records (Azazel, Callisto, Juggernaut, Lady Deathstrike). Marvel Database calls him Frederick Dukes (Earth-TRN872).

X-Men '97 episode 15 (S2E5 'Weapon X, Lies, and DVDs'): Wolverine recruits Sabretooth, Lady Deathstrike, Maverick and Kane for the Weapon X raid; Marvel Database lists him under Team X (Earth-92131) as a featured member. Lady Deathstrike's record already has Team X from X-Men '97 S2 for the same raid.

X-Men '97 episode 16 (S2E6 'Danger.Exe'): Carl Denti (the X-Cutioner) appears as a member of the Purifiers in their first appearance; Marvel Database gives his current affiliation as Purifiers, formerly Friends of Humanity.

He is already a student at Xavier's school in X-Men (2000) (Storm's class, the fireball Bobby freezes). The X-Men stage is keyed to X2, but the same student status that puts him in the X-Men in X2 holds from X-Men (2000); he only leaves for Magneto at Alkali Lake in X2.

In season 2 (episode 18, S2E9) she only teams up with Captain Carter against Strange Supreme, and the Watcher returns her home. She joins Carter's new Guardians of the Multiverse in season 3: the team (Carter, Kahhori, Byrdie, Storm) is first shown in S3E7 (episode 25), saving Earth-625 from the cosmic squid.

The S1 Guardians end in S1E9 when the Watcher sends everyone home. In S2E9 (episode 18) she works with Kahhori against Strange Supreme and the Watcher returns her to her world; no Guardians team exists in season 2. She forms the new Guardians of the Multiverse (Kahhori, Byrdie, Storm) 'sometime after parting ways with the Watcher', first shown in S3E7 (episode 25). Only the last stage's title changes, S2 to S3.

Stages are out of story order: the list puts him in the Hellfire Club before Nazi Germany. In First Class he is Dr. Klaus Schmidt working for the Nazis at Auschwitz in 1944, and founds the Hellfire Club afterwards (1950s Las Vegas club, leader by 1962). The leading Hellfire Club stage claims a membership before 1944 that never happens; the last stage is unchanged.

Stages are out of story order: Weapon X is listed first, before the U.S. Army. In Origins Victor fights in the Army through the wars, then joins Stryker's Team X, then works for Stryker's Weapon X program hunting former Team X members, and finally walks away (Independent). The last stage and the left title are unchanged.

Stages are out of story order: the leading Weapon X stage puts him in Weapon X before Team X. In Origins Wade Wilson is a Team X mercenary first, and only later does Stryker turn him into Weapon XI. The last stage is unchanged.

Stages are out of story order: the leading Yashida Corporation stage comes before the Imperial Japanese Army. He is an IJA soldier at Nagasaki in 1945 and only founds the Yashida Corporation in 1953. The last stage is unchanged.

The Red Room is her past: she defected and killed Dreykov before joining S.H.I.E.L.D. In episode 14 (S2E5, 'What If... Captain Carter Fought the Hydra Stomper?') she fights the Red Room alongside Peggy; she never rejoins it. Her S2 flashback shows her in the Avengers at the Battle of New York, and she ends the episode at Avengers Tower. The Red Room stage at S2 wrongly puts her back in the Red Room after S.H.I.E.L.D.

In episode 21 (S3E3, 'What If... the Red Guardian Stopped the Winter Soldier?'), Bill Foster recruits Shostakov to help the U.S. Twenty-one years later he joins the Avengers at the Battle of New York, pushing into their circle between Captain America and Black Widow. Marvel Database also lists his affiliation as Avengers.

This is the same Steve Rogers as A:by-steve-rogers-stomper, from Captain Carter's universe in 'What If...? S1E1' and episode 14 (S2E5). Marvel Database designates him Earth-82111. The villain file has null (main MCU), which is wrong.

Steve's U.S. Army, SSR and Howling Commandos stages all happen in episode 1 (S1E1, 'What If... Captain Carter Were the First Avenger?'), not S2. The twin file A:by-steve-rogers-stomper already dates them to S1. This file is only on file for S2, so the owner may prefer to keep S2 here.

Nothing returns Killmonger to the U.S. military after he becomes Black Panther (ep 6) and joins the Guardians of the Multiverse (ep 9). In ep 9 he turns on the Guardians to take Ultron's Stones and is trapped with Zola. In ep 18 Kahhori sends him back to his own world, and no group is shown. Marvel Database lists U.S. Navy, Stark Industries and the Guardians all as former affiliations. The last 'U.S. Military' stage has no source.

In What If...? ep 9 Killmonger turns on the Guardians of the Multiverse and attacks them for the Infinity Stones. That is a real departure (he turns on the group), and he joins no other group afterwards.

In What If...? ep 3 Hank Pym is not a S.H.I.E.L.D. member. He is a former agent, out since before the episode, who acts alone as Yellowjacket to avenge Hope's death on a S.H.I.E.L.D. mission. Marvel Database lists S.H.I.E.L.D. only as a former affiliation. No title on file shows him in S.H.I.E.L.D.
No departure happens on screen in What If...? ep 3. His break with S.H.I.E.L.D. is backstory, and he acts alone through the whole episode. Being caught by Fury and Loki is not leaving a group.

Marvel Database files Sibyl, the Chronicom Predictor from the main timeline's future (first seen AoS S7E3, killed S7E13 when Daisy destroys her ship), under Reality Earth-199999. The Earth-19859 pages are reserved for natives of the branched timeline, such as Nathaniel Malick (Earth-19859).

Strange Supreme never rejoins the Masters of the Mystic Arts. His universe is destroyed in S1E4. He joins the Guardians of the Multiverse in S1E8-9 and then stays alone in his dead universe, guarding Killmonger and Zola. Marvel Database lists his affiliation as Guardians of the Multiverse (current) and Masters of the Mystic Arts (former). In S3E8 he aids the new Guardians.

In Deadpool & Wolverine, Johnny is a member of the Void Resistance alongside Elektra, Blade, Gambit and Laura. He goes missing on a scouting run, and the Resistance learns from Wade and Logan that Cassandra Nova killed him. Marvel Database lists his affiliation as Resistance (Void), formerly the Fantastic Four.

Deadpool & Wolverine establishes, through dialogue only, that Matt was pruned to the Void, joined the Resistance against Cassandra Nova, and died defending Elektra. The record's own D&W step already names him among the Resistance dead. Marvel Database lists his affiliations as Nelson and Murdock and Resistance (Void).

Geoffrey is not part of Wizard in seasons 1–2 (it is the Minorus' company). In Runaways S3, after Catherine's death, he joins Wizard Computers under Morgan le Fay's spell (S3 episodes 6–7, 'RW306'/'RW307'), works against the Runaways, is freed after Dagger knocks him out (episode 8, RW308), and then reassembles PRIDE to rescue Molly (episode 9). Fandom lists Wizard as a former affiliation, joined in S3.
